speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're a newborn with respiratory distress; since you're an infant, I'll need to ask your caregiver a few questions to understand what symptoms you're seeing. Can you tell me how old the baby is and when these breathing difficulties started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Given the prematurity and the onset of distress within two hours, is there any history of meconium aspiration, and are you currently administering any supplemental oxygen or mechanical ventilation to the infant?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Gases: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L; Chest_Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).
